title: Feedback Tiling Scoutbook and Probe Checklist
content:
Purpose and framing:
This is a compact scoutbook for taking raw runtime feedback and 'tiling' it into manageable probe lanes we can run as low-effort experiments. The goal: turn noisy asks into reproducible probes that show impact (latency/cost/quality) and required lift.

How we tile feedback (quick method):
- Axes: user pain (customer impact) vs. operational cost (engineering effort + infra).
- Granularity: tile = a small, testable hypothesis (example: "expose KV cache hit rate per-api-key").
- Probe types: telemetry (+dash), UX workaround, config toggle, minimal server-side guardrail (fallback rule).

Summary of signals observed (sourced from CS threads + field interviews, Oct-Nov 2026):
- Frequent ask: visibility into per-request KV cache influence. Customers want to know when cache helped a long-running chat (billing and correctness reasons). Several enterprise users reported surprising cost spikes.
- Recurrent: more nuanced fallback controls. Teams want to route to cheaper quantized variants for background tasks but keep premium variants for low-latency bursts.
- Streaming reliability: a handful of customers reported partial streams when clients disconnect then reattach (want resume tokens / stable stream ids).
- Embedding drift: customers building similarity search want a simple way to pin an embedding model family and failover safely when a newer model changes vector geometry.
- Billing clarity: requests for token-breakdown by model variant when automatic fallback occurs.

Representative customer quotes (anonymized):
- "We had a day where our bill doubled — turns out cache wasn't firing for the new prompt prefix. We had zero visibility."
- "We'd pay for guaranteed latency on some routes, but need a one-line policy to tell you which requests are critical."

Prioritized tiles (quick ranking: expected impact / cost):
1) KV cache diagnostics tile (impact high / cost low)
   - Hypothesis: adding per-request cache-hit boolean + prefix length in logs will reduce next-day CS escalations by surfacing root cause faster.
   - Probe: add two log fields (cache_hit: true/false, cache_prefix_len: int) to debug-level request logs and sample them to 1% analytics stream.
   - Minimal success metric: CS ticket triage time down 30% in 2 weeks for incidents mentioning "cache".

2) Model-fallback billing attribution (impact medium-high / cost medium)
   - Hypothesis: if customers see per-token breakdown by effective model at time of token generation (even when fallback), disputes drop and customers adopt fallback for cost control.
   - Probe: create a per-request billing artifact (JSON) stored with request id containing token_count_by_model and include in billing export for 1 pilot customer.

3) Streaming resume token pilot (impact medium / cost low-medium)
   - Hypothesis: issuing an id + resume token at stream start allows clients to reattach and avoid duplicate generation; reduces dropped-response troubleshooting.
   - Probe: serve a non-breaking header (X-Stream-Resume: <id>) and implement server-side short-lived cache for incomplete sequences for 30s.

4) Embedding-pin + regression alert tile (impact medium / cost medium)
   - Hypothesis: allowing customers to pin embedding family and get an automated embedding drift score on each model update reduces latent search breakages.
   - Probe: add a pin flag to embedding route + small daily job computing centroid shift; send alert when cosine shift > threshold for pilot accounts.

Operational notes and dependencies:
- Telemetry changes for KV cache tile should go to debug stream only; product analytics must ensure PIIs are not leaked. Work with privacy to confirm sampling.
- Billing attribution requires a tiny storage artifact per-request; coordinate with billing infra (ENG-4127) for retention policy.
- Streaming resume token interacts with gateway connection handling in SRE; scope a 2-week spike.

Quick experiment plan (week-by-week snapshot):
Week 0: Align owners, pick 1 pilot customer for billing artifact; confirm data sampling for cache logs.
Week 1: Instrument KV cache debug fields; start 1% roll.
Week 2: Monitor CS tickets; do rapid retro; if signals positive, expand to 5%.
Week 3: Launch billing artifact pilot for 1 customer and collect feedback.
Week 4: Implement streaming resume header in canary; monitor failing stream rate.

Low-effort customer-facing artifacts to attach to probes:
- One-pager: "How KV cache affects billing" (short description + screenshots of debug fields).
- Quick-runbook for customers: "How to pin an embedding family" (2 steps).

Open questions / risks (notes to eng/product):
- Cost for storing per-request billing artifacts could grow; need TTL and coarse sampling for non-pilot accounts.
- Embedding-pin might give false safety; need clear messaging on drift detection vs. model quality.
- Resume token cache is a transient memory tax; SRE must set limits per-tenant.

Next steps (owners):
- Marceline Ortiz: coordinate pilot customer outreach + draft the one-pagers.
- Ethan Brooks: spike KV cache log fields (2d).
- Priya Shah: own billing artifact design + privacy review.
- Luca Romano: prototype streaming resume header in gateway stack.

Appendix: quick links and places to update if probe goes live:
- Confluence page: feedback-tiling-methodology (linked above)
- Jira epic: ENG-4127 (billing attribution)
- Slack thread: #feedback-tiling for rapid status updates

Notes to self: keep this doc short and use it as the living checklist for the next 6 weeks. Mark edits with initials and date (MO 2026-11-09).
